drug_class: Antiviral medication (Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitor - NRTI)
purpose: Lamivudine is used to treat HIV infection and chronic hepatitis B. For HIV, it is always used in combination with other HIV medicines to help control the virus. It helps keep your immune system healthier and lowers your risk of getting infections related to HIV or hepatitis B.
how_it_works: The HIV or hepatitis B virus needs to make copies of itself inside your body to survive. Lamivudine works by blocking a key tool the virus uses to copy itself, called reverse transcriptase. Think of it like putting a broken piece into a puzzle the virus is trying to build — it stops the copying process so the virus cannot spread as easily in your body.
common_side_effects: Headache, tiredness, nausea, diarrhea, stomach pain, trouble sleeping, and a general feeling of not feeling well. Most of these tend to get better after your body adjusts to the medication in the first few weeks.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor, especially if you have hepatitis B, as stopping can cause a serious flare-up of the infection. In rare cases, lamivudine can cause a dangerous build-up of lactic acid in the blood — tell your doctor right away if you feel very weak, have stomach pain, feel cold in your arms or legs, or have trouble breathing. Also let your doctor know if you have kidney problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
typical_dosing: For HIV in adults, the usual dose is 300 mg once a day or 150 mg twice a day, taken with or without food. For hepatitis B, the dose is typically 100 mg once a day. Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition, weight, and kidney function. Always take it exactly as prescribed and do not skip doses.
